chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from 'Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Humran, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: Do not eat the slaughtered meat of the Nāsib (one who bears enmity to the Ahl al-Bayt) unless you hear him mentioning (the name of God).

key_terms.النَّاصِبِ: the Nāsib (one who bears enmity, specifically to the Ahl al-Bayt)

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for eating meat slaughtered by the Nāsib according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Istibsar, Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), emphasizing that mere profession of Islam is insufficient for the meat of a 'Nāsib' (one with enmity towards the Ahl al-Bayt) to be considered halal; the explicit invocation of Allah's name (Tasmiyah) is a mandatory condition. This highlights the Shia jurisprudential focus on the spiritual and theological status of the slaughterer, linking ritual purity to doctrinal fidelity. The requirement ensures that the act of slaughter retains its religious validity despite the potential impurity of the individual's heart or allegiance.
